title: City Council District 5
statement: The first training cohort placement is a watershed moment for East Oakland—not because the numbers meet expectations, but because we're finally prioritizing our youth over bureaucracy. 62% approval tells me the people see what I see: that this program is the lifeline our community has been waiting for. But let's be clear—this isn't check-the-box workforce development. We're building real pathways out of poverty in a neighborhood with 31 violent crimes last cycle while the city averaged 23.9. I'm watching those placements like a hawk to ensure East Oakland's youth aren't getting scraps.

payload.text: The Baylight District corridor conditions demand immediate investment in safety infrastructure alongside apprenticeship opportunities—we won't solve one without the other. I'm calling for co-response teams to partner with cohort supervisors to secure routes to job sites.
